proofpoint_tap to OCSF pipeline.
Parses events, drops noise, maps to OCSF schema, and outputs compact JSON.

functions.description: Parse Proofpoint TAP JSON envelope into top-level fields
Normalize array fields to scalars and map core identity fields
Extract first threat details from threatsInfoMap array
Derive action, direction, and vendor_action from quarantine and policy state

add.name: severity
add.value: (malwareScore >= 90 || (impostorScore >= 9 && phishScore >= 80)) ? 'critical' : (phishScore >= 75 || malwareScore >= 50 || impostorScore >= 8) ? 'high' : (phishScore >= 30 || spamScore >= 50 || impostorScore >= 3) ? 'medium' : (spamScore >= 10 || phishScore > 0) ? 'low' : 'info'

functions.description: Classify severity from malware/phish/impostor scores and quarantine folder
Alias captured timestamp field(s) to log_time (timestamp, threat_time) so _time reflects the source event, not pipeline processing time

findings.issue: OCSF class_uid 4001 is Email Activity — the entire email object is missing. No from, to, subject, message_id, size, reply_to, or any email-specific fields mapped despite all being present in source.
findings.example: source has subject='URGENT: Outstanding Invoice #INV-2024-8821', recipient=['cfo@targetcorp.com'], sender='billing@fakeinvoice-domain.ru' — none appear in output

findings.issue: severity_id is null across all events despite rich scoring data (phishScore, malwareScore, impostorScore, spamScore) available to derive a severity. OCSF requires a valid severity_id integer.
findings.example: event 1: phishScore=95, malwareScore=100 → should map to severity_id 5 (Critical) or similar; output has null

findings.issue: threatsInfoMap with threat details (threatID, threatType, threatStatus, threatUrl, threat value) is completely dropped. This is the primary threat intelligence payload of TAP events.
findings.example: source: threatsInfoMap=[{threat:'http://fakeinvoice-domain.ru/pay/8821', threatID:'abc123def456', threatType:'url', threatStatus:'active'}] — absent in output

findings.issue: actor.user is an empty object. sender email address and fromAddress are present in source and should populate actor.user.email_addr at minimum.
dst_endpoint is empty. recipient/toAddresses are present in source and should map to dst_endpoint or email.to fields.
Quarantine disposition data (quarantineFolder, quarantineRule) is entirely dropped. These map to OCSF disposition or action fields and are critical for email security events.
findings.example: source quarantineFolder='Phish', quarantineRule='phish_high_confidence' — absent in output

findings.issue: The Proofpoint event UUID (id field) is not mapped to any OCSF identifier field such as uid or metadata.uid.
clusterId identifying the Proofpoint cluster is dropped, should map to metadata.product.uid or similar.
Product name is set to generic 'Security' instead of 'Targeted Attack Protection' or 'TAP' which accurately reflects Proofpoint TAP.
policyRoutes and modulesRun arrays are present in all source events but not mapped to any OCSF field (e.g., policy or enrichment arrays).
All four ML scoring fields from TAP are dropped. These are key risk indicators and should map to risk_score or enrichment data within OCSF.
findings.example: source impostorScore=9.2, phishScore=88 for BEC event — absent in output

findings.issue: URL rewriting flag (completelyRewritten) dropped — relevant to action taken on the email.
Email header fields (xmailer, headerFrom, headerReplyTo) present in source are not mapped.
findings.example: source xmailer='MailChimp', headerFrom='"Retail News" <newsletter@legitimate-retailer.com>' — absent in output

findings.issue: connection_info and traffic are present as empty objects — these stubs add no value and should either be populated or omitted.
device is an empty object with no mappable source data — should be omitted if nothing populates it.

report.summary: The pipeline extracts only the sender IP into src_endpoint and correctly sets timestamps and basic OCSF structural fields (class_uid 4001, category_uid 4). However, the vast majority of the rich Proofpoint TAP payload — email headers, recipients, subject, threat intelligence (threatsInfoMap), risk scores, quarantine disposition, event UUID, and policy routes — is entirely dropped. With OCSF class 4001 being Email Activity, the absence of any email object is a critical structural failure. Only approximately 3-4 fields out of ~30 available source fields are mapped, resulting in a very low score.
